items.prompt: Game A, move 8, White to move. Both sides are castled and the centre is closed. Three plans: finish development with a quiet move, strike at once with d4, or pin the knight with Bg5. Play the move you prefer.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is Nbd2, h3 or b4, and all three are within 40 centipawns of it.
At depth 16 the strike d4 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move.
The black pawn on h6 attacks g5, so a bishop landing there is taken.
At depth 16 Bg5 is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Look at g5 and at d4. How many black pieces and pawns attack each square after you play there?
Bg5 can be taken by a pawn. Is d4 ready before the last knight is out? Which plans are left?
Finish development: the knight to d2, or a waiting move such as h3 or b4.
items.explain: Quiet development keeps every white piece guarded. The strike d4 scores at least 40 centipawns lower at depth 16, and Bg5 simply loses the bishop to the pawn on h6. The move b4 also scores within 10 centipawns of the best at depth 16, but it offers a pawn, so the lesson prefers the quiet moves; it counts as correct here.

feedback_by_move.d3d4: d4 is a fine break in other positions, but here it scores at least 40 centipawns worse than a quiet move at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.c1g5: The pawn on h6 attacks g5, so the bishop is simply taken.

items.prompt: White to move on move 10. Black's knight on g4 and bishop on c5 both aim at f2. Three ideas: hit the knight with h3, guard f2 with the rook, or strike with d4. Play your choice.

claims.statement: Two black pieces attack f2.
Only one white piece (the king) defends f2.
At depth 16 the engine's best move is Re2 or Rf1, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.
At depth 16 h3 is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 d4 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of f2 before you move anything.
f2 is attacked twice and defended once. A move that adds a defender comes first; a move that chases the knight does not.
The rook can slide along the first or second rank to guard f2.
items.explain: f2 is attacked twice and defended once, so the pawn is the problem to solve first. A rook move adds a defender; h3 loses to ...Nxf2, and d4 scores at least 40 centipawns worse.

feedback_by_move.h2h3: h3 attacks the knight but ignores f2: ...Nxf2 wins the pawn with a discovered attack. At depth 16 h3 is at least 300 centipawns worse than the rook moves.
feedback_by_move.d3d4: d4 opens the centre while f2 is still weak. At depth 16 it scores at least 40 centipawns worse than the rook moves.

items.prompt: White to move after 10...Kh8. Which plan fits?

options: Quiet piece moves, d4 later
Break with d4 right now
Storm the kingside with g4

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is h3, b4 or Bb3, all quiet, and all three are within 40 centipawns of it.
At depth 16 the strike d4 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move here.

hints: Test d4 first: how does the engine rate it compared with the quiet moves?
d4 now loses a lot. The moves the engine likes are all waiting or improving moves. Which plan is that?
Improve a piece and keep the d4 break for later.
items.explain: At depth 16 the quiet moves h3, b4 and Bb3 are all within 40 centipawns of the best, while d4 is at least a pawn worse. The break needs a moment when Black's pieces have left the centre.

items.prompt: White to move on move 12. Find one of the two strongest moves.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is d4 or Bd5, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.
At depth 16 the capture exf5 is at least 60 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 the capture hxg4 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move.
After d4 a white pawn attacks both c5 and e5.

hints: Which Black pieces are far from the centre now? A central pawn move may hit two things at once.
A pawn on d4 would attack the bishop on c5 and the pawn on e5. The pawn captures on f5 and g4 give Black something back.
Play d4, or the bishop move Bd5.
items.explain: d4 attacks the bishop and the e5 pawn together, and at depth 16 it is one of the two best moves. The captures exf5 and hxg4 score at least 40 and 60 centipawns worse.

feedback_by_move.e4f5: At depth 16 taking on f5 scores at least 60 centipawns worse than d4 or Bd5.
feedback_by_move.h3g4: At depth 16 taking the knight at once scores at least 40 centipawns worse than d4 or Bd5.

items.prompt: Black to move on move 13. White has just taken the knight on g4. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is fxg4.
At depth 16 the push d3 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 the capture fxe4 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.
Two white pieces attack the black pawn on d4.

hints: After you move, can White capture something for free? Check each of your three candidates.
The pawn on d4 is attacked, but the loose pawn on g4 is the one that matters. Recapturing first keeps the material close.
Take the pawn back with the f-pawn: fxg4.
items.explain: Recapturing with the f-pawn is the engine's choice at depth 16. The pawn push d3 scores at least 50 centipawns worse, and fxe4 at least a pawn worse.

feedback_by_move.d4d3: d3 attacks the rook, but the bishop simply takes the pawn. At depth 16 it is at least 50 centipawns worse than recapturing on g4.
feedback_by_move.f5e4: At depth 16 taking on e4 is at least 100 centipawns worse than recapturing on g4.

items.prompt: Black to move on move 15. Find the move the engine prefers.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is g3.
At depth 16 the trade Nxd4 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.
One white piece attacks c6.
One black piece defends c6.

hints: Taking the knight on d4 looks natural. What does White gain from the recapture cxd4?
After Nxd4 cxd4 the pawn attacks the bishop on c5. Black has other tries: the pawn on g4 can advance.
Push the pawn on with g3.
items.explain: The natural trade Nxd4 scores at least a pawn worse than the best move. Pushing the pawn on with g3 keeps the attack going, but White still stands better (about +1.6) [I]: the repair limits the damage, it does not equalise.

feedback_by_move.c6d4: Nxd4 cxd4 attacks the bishop on c5 with a pawn. At depth 16 it scores at least 100 centipawns worse than g3.

answer.outcome: White, by more than two pawns
options: White, by more than two pawns

Black, by more than one pawn

A white bishop stands on d3.

A black bishop stands on c8.

Count the minor pieces: White has three, Black two. Then count the pawns: Black has two more.
White is clearly better.

items.prompt: Black to move on move 6. The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6. Three replies: strike back with d5, jump with Ne4, or jump with Ng4. Play your choice.

claims.statement: A white pawn attacks f6.
At depth 16 the engine's best move is d5.
At depth 16 Ne4 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 Ng4 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Your knight is attacked by a pawn. Retreat is not the only answer: attack the bishop on c4.
A pawn on d5 attacks the bishop on c4 and blocks the e-pawn. The knight jumps give White more tempi.
Play the pawn: d5.
items.explain: d5 attacks the bishop and blocks the white pawn at once. At depth 16 it is the engine's best move, and both knight jumps are at least 50 centipawns worse.

feedback_by_move.f6e4: Ne4 gets the knight to a central square, but it does not deal with the bishop on c4. At depth 16 it scores at least 50 centipawns worse than d5.
feedback_by_move.f6g4: Ng4 runs to the rim of the board. At depth 16 it scores at least 50 centipawns worse than d5.

items.prompt: Black to move after 10.Be3. White's pawns on d4 and e5 form a chain, and the pawn on e5 is its head. Which plan fits?

answer.class: Pin the knight on f3 with the bishop
options: Pin the knight on f3 with the bishop
Push the queenside pawns, ...a5 and ...b6
Bring the queen to e7 to pile up on e5

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is Bg4 or f5, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.
At depth 16 the queen move Qe7 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 a5 is at least 25 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 the game move f6 is at least 25 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Look at the pawn chain. Where does a chain break most easily?
A chain is weakened by attacking what supports it. Which black piece move bothers the knight that guards the centre?
The best moves are the pin ...Bg4 and the lever ...f5; the options list only the pin.
items.explain: At depth 16 the pin Bg4 and the lever f5 are the best moves. Qe7 loses at least a pawn and a5 at least 25 centipawns. The game move f6, a lever on e5, was a little behind, within the noise of engine runs (about a quarter-pawn or less).

items.prompt: White to move on move 15 after ...Bxf3. Recapture with the bishop or with the pawn on g2?

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is Bxf3.
At depth 16 gxf3 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.
After Bxf3 only White holds the bishop pair.

hints: Count what each recapture does to the pawn structure and to the pair of bishops.
Recapturing with the pawn doubles White's f-pawns; recapturing with the bishop keeps both bishops.
Take with the bishop.
items.explain: Bxf3 keeps the pawns healthy and leaves White the only side with two bishops. gxf3 doubles the pawns and scores at least a pawn worse at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.g2f3: gxf3 doubles White's pawns on the f-file. At depth 16 it scores at least 100 centipawns worse than Bxf3.

items.prompt: White to move after 12...Qxf6. Which description fits the pawn structure?

answer.class: Pawns on c3 and d4 against d5; the e-file is open; White has a lone a-pawn
options: Pawns on c3 and d4 against d5; the e-file is open; White has a lone a-pawn
A closed centre with locked chains and no open file
A symmetrical structure with all eight pawns each

claims.statement: The e-file is open; the b-file is half-open for White and the f-file for Black.
White has three pawn islands.
Black has two pawn islands.

hints: Count each side's pawns and then ask which files have no pawns.
Neither side has all eight pawns, and there is an open file. Which description matches?
The first option.
items.explain: White has three pawn islands to Black's two, the e-file is open, and White's a-pawn stands alone, so the first description fits.

items.prompt: Black to move on move 21. Find a strong move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is Nc4 or Qf7, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.
At depth 16 Qf3 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which Black piece has the worst square, and which move leaves the kingside undefended?
A queen that leaves the defence of the kingside for a tempting central post can be harassed with tempo.
Play the knight back into the game with Nc4, or keep the queen home with Qf7.
items.explain: Nc4 and Qf7 both keep Black close to the best play (about +0.5 and +0.7 for White at depth 16, one run). Qf3 looks active but scores at least a pawn worse.

feedback_by_move.f6f3: Qf3 looks active, but at depth 16 it is at least 100 centipawns worse than Nc4.

items.prompt: White to move on move 22. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is Qh3.
At depth 16 Qxf3 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 h3 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Look at the two queens. Is a queen trade what White wants when the attack on the king is alive?
The queen can step back to h3 and keep the bishop and the queen aimed at h7.
Play Qh3.
items.explain: Qh3 keeps both queens on the board and the attack on h7 alive. Trading queens with Qxf3 scores at least 50 centipawns worse, and the pawn move h3 at least a pawn worse at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.g4f3: At depth 16 trading queens scores at least 50 centipawns worse than Qh3.
feedback_by_move.h2h3: At depth 16 the pawn move h3 scores at least 100 centipawns worse than Qh3.

options: yes
no

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is d4 or Bd5, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.

hints: Where is Black's knight? Where is Black's king? Are those pieces near the centre?
Black's knight stands on g4 and the king on h8, both far from the pawn on e5.
Yes, d4 is sound here.
items.explain: d4 attacks the bishop and the pawn on e5 at once and is one of the two best moves at depth 16 (about +0.8 for White). It works because the capture on g4 is possible: the knight stands there.

items.prompt: White to move. Is the break d4 among the engine's best moves here?

options: yes

claims.statement: At depth 16 d4 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move.
At depth 16 the engine's best move is Nh4.

hints: Compare Black's knight with the previous position. Where is it now?
On g4 the knight could be won by a pawn capture. Can that happen with the knight on f6?
No: without the capture on g4, d4 wins nothing and a quiet move is better.
items.explain: With the knight on f6 the capture hxg4 is not possible, so d4 wins no piece. At depth 16 d4 is at least 40 centipawns (about 0.7 of a pawn here) worse than the best move, though the position stays roughly level [I].
